definition: Data engineering is a software engineering approach to the building of data systems, to enable the collection and usage of data.
details: This data is usually used to enable subsequent analysis and data science, which often involves machine learning. Making the data usable usually involves substantial computing and storage, as well as data processing.

explainer.lead: Data engineering turns raw data into something people and software can reliably use. It supplies the systems, processing, computing, and storage needed for later analysis, data science, and machine learning.

tiers.eli5: Imagine collecting LEGO pieces from different boxes, sorting them, removing broken ones, and putting them into labeled drawers. Data engineering does a similar job for information so that other people can study it or use it to teach computers. Without that preparation, useful pieces would be hard to find and use.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build data systems that collect, process, and store data for analysis and machine learning. Their work must make data usable while accounting for substantial computing and storage needs. A common pitfall is treating downstream analysis as the whole job and underestimating the processing needed to prepare its inputs.
tiers.paperLevel: Data engineering is a software engineering approach to constructing data systems that enable data collection and usage. In plain-text notation: data systems = collection + processing + computing + storage, supporting downstream analysis, data science, and often machine learning. Its central concern is making data usable before that downstream work occurs.

explainer.example: An online shop collects records of customer purchases. Its data system processes those records and stores the usable result, which a data scientist can then analyze or use as input to a machine-learning system.

usedIn.name: Data analysis
usedIn.detail: Provides collected and processed data that analysts can use.

usedIn.name: Data science
usedIn.detail: Builds the systems that make data available and usable for data-science work.

usedIn.name: Machine learning
usedIn.detail: Supplies processed data for machine-learning applications.

explainer.intuition: Useful analysis depends on more than having data: the data must be collected, processed, and stored in a usable form. Data engineering applies software engineering to building the systems that do this.
howItWorks: Collect data in a data system.
Process the data to make it usable.
Provide the computing and storage the data requires.
Make the result available for analysis, data science, or machine learning.
explainer.whyItMatters: Analysis and machine learning cannot make effective use of data that remains difficult to access or process. Data engineering provides the foundation that makes subsequent work possible.
misconceptions: Data engineering is not the same as data analysis; it builds the systems that enable analysis.
It is not merely storing data; making data usable also involves processing and computing.
